issue_context.title: Synthetic source implementation for `constant_keyword` is inconsistent with stored source
issue_context.body: Currently synthetic source for `constant_keyword` field is implemented to always write the constant value in `_source`. Most of the time such a value was not actually provided in the document (there is no reason to do that, it's constant) and therefore would not be in stored `_source`. This is problematic when using `constant_keyword` fields as a metadata fields that can be different between indices (f.e. reindexing an index into an index that has a different value of such a field). This scenario works with stored source since the values are never there but fails with synthetic source.
comments: I think `constand_keyword` fields can be completely skipped in synthetic source. When reindexed they will have the correct value anyway.

Alternatively we can use fallback synthetic source which will preserve the value if it is ever present in document. I can't imagine a scenario when that is important but it is closer to stored source behavior.

> Alternatively we can use fallback synthetic source which will preserve the value if it is ever present in document. I can't imagine a scenario when that is important but it is closer to stored source behavior.

Let's do that for now, the goal is to be on par with stored source.
@lkts lemme know if you don't have cycles to fix this.

review_comments: Maybe in a follow up we can extend `DataGenerationHelper` to use constant keyword? That we would test this with reindex too in `ReindexChallengeRestIT` subclasses.
